title: Surge forensics + soft-throttle playbook (field notes, WIP)
content:
PURPOSE
This is a living field-note playbook for fast containment of client-facing surge events that look like credential/fingerprint leaks or large-scale automated scrapers. Focus: buy time with soft throttles and targeted WAF quick rules while preserving legitimate traffic and key customers.

SCOPE / WHEN TO USE
- Sudden spike in 5xx/latency accompanied by anomalous per-key throughput (10x baseline)
- New 1xx-3xx client populations exhibiting uniform REST patterns (same path, same payload shape)
- Alerts: Token-exhaustion alarms, burst-queue-backpressure, account gating metrics crossing thresholds

Quick triage rubric (oncall checklist)
1) Confirm signal validity (5m)
   - Check traffic spike in edge NGWs and api-proxy logs (time-series).
   - Validate that spike correlates to specific API keys or small set of IPs/cidrs.
   - Confirm not an infra-side regression (deploy metadata, version header changes in request traces).
2) Identify scope (10m)
   - Which routes are hot? /v1/generate vs /v1/embeddings vs static content endpoints.
   - Top N API keys by requests in the last 15m (api-key-usage dashboard / Kibana).
   - Top N client IPs and ASNs.
3) Apply containment (15m)
   - Soft throttle: apply per-key token-bucket rate limit at 50% of observed median to buy time. Use adjustable gradation.
   - Targeted WAF rule: add a temporary rule to block the most egregious path/pattern (attach rule id).
   - Canary responses: send 429 with structured JSON pointing to status page when throttled for known integrations.

Fingerprinting steps (forensics ongoing)
- Request signature extraction: take top 200 request samples and compute fingerprints for headers, user-agent strings, sequence length, typical prompt prefixes. Store artifact in /incidents/SRE-4123/requests-samples.json.
- Sequence-distinctiveness score: compare token-length distribution to known customer baselines.
- KV cache hit rates: check for abnormal low cache reuse (indicates many distinct prompts).

Containment knobs (how to change safely)
- Soft throttle (recommended first): reduce per-key qps by 25% increments. Endpoint: internal admin API POST /admin/ratelimits/apply with body {\"scope\":\"key\",\"id\":\"<key-id>\",\"limit\":\"<rps>\"}
  - Rationale: less risky to legitimate users; immediate effect on overall token burn.
- Route-level circuit (next): apply route-based burst limits for /v1/generate to preserve control-plane stability.
- WAF quick-rule: block specific path+ua+ip patterns. Use WAF console rule name prefixed with sresurge-<YYYYMMDD>-<short>. Keep rules timeboxed (max 4h).
- Credential quarantine: if a single API key is clearly exfiltrated and abused, set state to QUARANTINED (not revoked) and notify account owner. Quarantine keeps read-only access for troubleshooting but denies write/generation.

Signaling & customer-facing behavior
- Response codes: prefer 429 with X-RateLimit headers instead of 403 to avoid escalation for unknown clients. Include Retry-After and diagnostic-code to surface in logs.
- Status page: open an incident in Statuspage and update entry with "mitigations in place; working with affected customers".

Quick commands (internal)
- Top keys: curl -sS 'https://telemetry.internal/api/keys?since=15m' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' | jq '.top_keys[0:10]'
- Apply soft throttle to key: curl -X POST 'https://admin.internal/api/ratelimit' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"scope":"key","id":"k_ABC123","limit_rps":25,"note":"auto-surge-soft-throttle-20260210"}'
- Add temporary WAF rule: use console -> waf -> add rule -> name sresurge-20260210-block-ua-bot -> condition: ua contains "curl/" and path startsWith "/v1/generate" and ip in X (ASN)

Escalation criteria (when to revoke soft throttle and go to hard blocks)
- If abuse persists after 30 minutes and median latency still >2x, escalate to per-ip hard block for top 5 IPs and set quota to 0 for clearly leaked keys (with legal/CS signoff).
- If telemetry shows evasion (UA rotates rapidly), move to pattern-based WAF rules (payload token prefix signatures) and require devs to add stronger client auth for affected customers.

Observability + post-action validation
- Dashboards to monitor after action: 5xx rate, p99 latency, token burn rate, queue depth for each slot. Watch for unintended collateral damage: drop in warm-key users or enterprise accounts.
- Verify logs (s3:/prod-logs/YYYY/MM/DD/requests) for 429 spikes and check that legitimate clients receive Retry-After headers.

Communication templates (oncall edit before sending)
- Slack short: "SRE: applying soft throttle to 3 keys and temporary WAF rule sresurge-20260210-block-ua-bot to contain automated surge. Monitoring impact; will update in 15m. Ticket SRE-4123."
- Customer DM (CS): "We observed anomalous traffic on your key and temporarily reduced request throughput to protect stability. We will restore once verified; reply if you need immediate change."

Audit & retention
- All temporary rules must be annotated with incident id and revert ETA. Create GitHub issue with mitigation steps and timeline.
- Store samples and rule snapshots to /incidents/SRE-4123/artifacts and tag in S3 for 90 days.

Post-incident analysis prompts (for retrospective)
- Root cause hypotheses: leaked API key vs malicious reseller vs broken client retry loop. Which evidence points where?
- Detection gaps: how quickly did dashboards show the per-key skew? Could an ML-based anomaly detector have detected earlier?
- Controls: should we add per-key spike alerts (per-key z-score) or an automated soft-throttle circuit?
- WAF: which quick-rule conditions worked and which caused false positives?

Unresolved questions (TODOs)
- How to perform safe automated quarantining for keys with unresolved customer identity? (legal/privilege check)
- Should we reduce default per-key burst limits at signup to make abuse costlier? (product + biz impact)
- Post-incident: convert successful quick rules into permanent mitigations or telemetry signals?

After-action checklist (assign owners)
- [ ] Save top 100 request samples to incidents bucket (owner: Mateo)
- [ ] Re-run fingerprint clustering and label likely actors (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Draft customer-facing note for affected enterprise (owner: CS lead)
- [ ] Propose an alert rule for per-key z-score > 6 (owner: infra-metrics)
- [ ] Remove temp WAF rules (owner: oncall) and verify rule count equals pre-incident (owner: oncall)

Notes to self: keep throttles reversible, prefer 429 over 403 in ambiguous cases, and timebox WAF rules. Capture as many raw request samples as permitted by PII policy; prefer hashing prompt contents with salted hash for signature work.

ANNEX: sample structured 429 body policy (copy into config)
{
  "code": "rate_limited",
  "message": "Request temporarily rate limited to protect service stability. See status.redwood.ai for updates.",
  "retry_after_seconds": 60,
  "diagnostic": "sresurge-20260210"
}

END OF FIELD NOTES (WIP)
Add updates here as we learn what rule combos are most surgical.
